questionText: Read the following sentences carefully, choose the one that is grammatically and contextually correct, and mark it as your answer.

options.text: The train had already left before we reached the station.
He is one of those players who works very hard every day.
Neither of the girls have submitted their reports yet.
She asked me that where I was going.
The flowers in the garden smells wonderful.

solutionExplanation: The correct answer is option 1. Key Points To answer this question, let's analyze each option: Option 1: The train had already left before we reached the station. This sentence is grammatically correct and contextually makes sense as it describes a past event using the past perfect tense ("had already left") and the simple past tense ("reached"). This is the correct answer. Option 2: He is one of those players who works very hard every day. This sentence is grammatically incorrect because the verb "works" should be "work" to agree with the plural subject "players" in the clause. The corrected sentence would be: "He is one of those players who work very hard every day." Option 3: Neither of the girls have submitted their reports yet. This sentence is grammatically incorrect because "neither" is singular and should be followed by "has" instead of "have." The corrected sentence would be: "Neither of the girls has submitted their reports yet." Option 4: She asked me that where I was going. This sentence is grammatically incorrect because "that" is unnecessary in indirect speech. The correct sentence should omit "that." The corrected sentence would be: "She asked me where I was going." Option 5: The flowers in the garden smells wonderful. This sentence is grammatically incorrect because the subject "flowers" is plural and should take the plural verb "smell" instead of "smells." The corrected sentence would be: "The flowers in the garden smell wonderful." Therefore, the grammatically and contextually correct sentence is option 1: "The train had already left before we reached the station."

Directions: In each of the following sentences, four words given in bold are marked as A, B, C, and D, which are possible pairs to be interchanged. Choose the pair(s) of words that need to be interchanged to make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful. If no interchange is required, mark option 5 (i.e., "No interchange required") as your answer.

As artificial intelligence tools become increasingly indispensable (A), many manual coding practices are rendered redundant (B), forcing software developers to adopt cutting-edge (C) frameworks to avoid becoming obsolete (D)
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is: Option 5 (No interchange required).

Key Points

  • The word "indispensable" means absolutely necessary or essential. (अनिवार्य/अपरिहार्य)
    • Example: Computers have become an indispensable part of modern office life.
  • The word "redundant" means no longer needed or useful; superfluous. (अनावश्यक/फालतू)
    • Example: The new automated system made several manual data entry tasks redundant.
  • The word "cutting-edge" refers to the latest or most advanced stage in the development of something. (अत्याधुनिक)
    • Example: The laboratory is equipped with cutting-edge technology for genetic research.
  • The word "obsolete" means no longer produced or used; out of date. (अप्रचलित/पुराना)
    • Example: With the rise of digital streaming, physical DVDs are rapidly becoming obsolete.
  • Contextual logic:
    • The sentence describes a logical progression in the tech industry: AI tools are becoming necessary (indispensable), which makes old manual ways unnecessary (redundant).
    • As a result, developers must use advanced (cutting-edge) tools so that they themselves do not become irrelevant/outdated (obsolete).
    • Since all bolded words are used correctly according to their definitions and the sentence's context, no interchange is necessary.

Therefore, the correct answer is- Option 5 (No interchange required).

Additional Information

Here is why the other interchange options are incorrect:

  • A-C: Swapping these would mean AI tools are "cutting-edge" (which is okay) but developers adopt "indispensable" frameworks. While possible, "indispensable" doesn't fit the "adopt... to avoid becoming" structure as well as "cutting-edge" does.
  • B-D: Swapping these would mean practices are rendered "obsolete" and developers avoid becoming "redundant." While these are synonyms, "rendered redundant" is a more standard colocation in professional contexts regarding tasks.
  • A-D: Swapping these would result in AI tools becoming "obsolete," which contradicts the premise that they are forcing developers to change their practices.
  • B-C: Swapping these would mean practices are rendered "cutting-edge," which makes no sense if the goal is to "avoid becoming obsolete."

solutionExplanation:

Key Points

  • The word "antagonistic" refers to showing or feeling active opposition or hostility toward someone or something. (विरोधी/शत्रुतापूर्ण)
    • Example: The two neighbors have had an antagonistic relationship for years over a boundary dispute.
  • The correct word "diplomatic" refers to being sensitive and tactful in dealing with people, especially in international relations. (राजनयिक/कुशल)
    • Example: The secretary gave a diplomatic response to avoid offending either of the two parties.
  • Contextual logic:
    • The sentence mentions that a belligerent (hostile) tone was "unexpected," which implies the ambassador's usual behavior is peaceful and tactful.
    • Therefore, her "usual approach" would involve diplomatic (D) negotiations and conciliatory (C) gestures.
    • Conversely, a threat is better described as antagonistic (B) rather than "diplomatic."
    • By interchanging B and D, the sentence becomes: "...her usual approach strictly involved diplomatic (D) negotiations and conciliatory (C) gestures rather than antagonistic (B) threats."

Therefore, the correct answer is- Option 2 (B-D).

Additional Information

Here are the explanations for the remaining bolded words:

  • Belligerent (युद्धप्रिय/आक्रामक): Hostile and aggressive; engaged in a war or conflict.
    • Example: The nation's belligerent rhetoric toward its neighbors sparked concerns of an impending invasion.
  • Conciliatory (समझौतापूर्ण/मैत्रीपूर्ण): Intended or likely to placate or pacify.
    • Example: After the heated argument, he made a conciliatory phone call to apologize and settle the matter.

The renowned philosopher posited that human suffering is not merely a perpetual (A) anomaly but an inherent (B) facet of mortal existence, whereas the happiness we chase is often an extraneous (C) illusion rather than a transient (D) state
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is: Option 4 (A-D) i.e. 'A-D'.

Key Points

  • The word "perpetual" means never ending or changing; occurring repeatedly so as to seem endless. (अनवरत/स्थायी)
    • Example: The deep caves are in a state of perpetual darkness, as sunlight never reaches them.
  • The correct word "transient" refers to something that lasts only for a short time; impermanent. (क्षणभंगुर/अल्पकालिक)
    • Example: The joy of winning the game was transient, as the team soon had to focus on the next difficult match.
  • Contextual logic:
    • The sentence uses the phrase "not merely a... but an..." to create a contrast between a minor/temporary thing and an essential/permanent one. An "anomaly" (deviation from the norm) is logically described as transient (D) (passing or temporary) rather than "perpetual" (everlasting).
    • In the second part of the sentence, the philosopher contrasts happiness with suffering. If suffering is "inherent" (permanent), then the happiness we chase is contrasted as not being a perpetual (A) (everlasting) state, but rather an illusion.
    • By interchanging A and D, the sentence becomes philosophically and logically sound: "...suffering is not merely a transient (D) anomaly but an inherent (B) facet... whereas happiness... is an illusion rather than a perpetual (A) state."

Therefore, the correct answer is- Option 4 (A-D).

Additional Information

Here are the explanations for the remaining bolded words in the sentence:

  • Inherent (निहित/स्वाभाविक): Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.
    • Example: There are inherent risks in any startup venture, no matter how well-planned it is.
  • Extraneous (बाहरी/अप्रासंगिक): Irrelevant or unrelated to the subject being dealt with; of external origin.
    • Example: When writing a summary, you should exclude extraneous details and focus only on the main points.

This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct. Therefore, the correct answer is option 5.
